analysis.investment_thesis: Delhivery is a logistics company that just earned INR 162 Cr of net profit in FY25 — its first profitable year — and is priced at INR 34,676 Cr market cap (192x trailing P/E). Paying 214x earnings for a thin-margin logistics business with no promoter holding and no identifiable economic moat is speculation, not investing.
key_strengths: Revenue has grown at 32.5% CAGR since FY19 — genuine scale has been built across India's express parcel network
Low debt (D/E 0.17) and large equity base (INR 9,529 Cr) mean the balance sheet can absorb continued investment
OCF turned firmly positive in FY24-25, suggesting the unit economics are finally inflecting
key_risks: ROE of 1.52% and ROCE of 2.47% are catastrophically low — capital is not being rewarded at any acceptable rate
Logistics is a brutally competitive, low-moat industry; Blue Dart, Ecom Express, and Shadowfax all compete for the same shipments
No promoter holding (FII 48.57%, DII 34.98%) means no owner-operator with skin in the game
red_flags: Cumulative losses from FY19–FY24 totalled over INR 4,700 Cr — the business consumed vast capital before approaching breakeven
EV/EBITDA of -767.8x (still negative on a prior-period basis) and 192x P/E reflect purely speculative pricing
Operating margin of 0.79% means any volume shortfall or fuel cost spike wipes out the thin profit layer entirely
analysis.detailed_analysis:
I have spent my career avoiding businesses that require perpetual capital injections to survive. Delhivery required over a decade of venture and IPO funding before printing its first modest profit of INR 162 Cr. The gross margin of 83.65% looks attractive until you realise that the entire cost structure is variable and labour-intensive — a characteristic of service businesses without pricing power, not businesses like Coca-Cola.

The implied valuation of INR 34,676 Cr on INR 162 Cr of net profit assumes a decade of flawless execution in an industry I regard as one of the most competitive and capital-destructive. With no promoter anchor, no economic moat, and returns on capital barely above zero, there is no price at which I would find this interesting today.
